newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ruehe demands German cash for Eurofighter in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Ruehe demands German cash for Eurofighter in 1998.

text.p: German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe was quoted on Wednesday saying that the Bonn government must set aside cash from next year's budget to finance start-up production of the Eurofighter combat jet.
"Despite all our financial problems, we must make available the first funds when we draft the 1998 budget in July," Ruehe told the Hannoversche Allgemeine newspaper.

Ruehe had pressed Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet to make a decision to fund the purchase of 180 Eurofighters by the end of March. But with Bonn struggling to cut borrowing to qualify for Europe's single currency, a decision has been put on ice.

Eurofighter project partners Britain and Spain have made commitments to buy the multi-role Eurofighter. The British Labour party, leading in opinion polls ahead of a May 1 general election, has also pledged to back the project.
Ruehe told the newspaper failure to buy the Eurofighter would leave Germany will a hopelessly outdated air force.
The option of buying from the U.S. would only worsen the Germany's jobs crisis. "Who in the current situation undermines investment is doing the wrong thing," he said.
The Eurofighter's German partner, Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG, has said that the future of 18,000 jobs depends on building the combat jet.
The other partners in the project are British Aerospace, Alenia Spa of Italy and Spain's state-owned CASA.
Ruehe had negotiated a price tag of 23 billion marks for the batch of Eurofighters Bonn wants to buy, pricing each aircraft at 125.4 million marks.

The opposition Social Democrats (SPD) say the money could be better spent elsewhere. Finance spokeswoman Ingrid Matthaeus-Maier told German radio that the SPD would vote against buying Eurofighter in parliament.
